recent_posts.title: Backstage in Amsterdam: Highlights from BackstageCon and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026
recent_posts.summary: A recap of Backstage's presence at BackstageCon and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026 in Amsterdam. Highlights include a full day of community talks covering IDP governance at large organizations (Booking.com, ING Bank, N26), the world premiere of the Backstage Documentary, a standing-room-only State of Backstage session with 600+ attendees covering the new Frontend System and upcoming MCP/AI-native features, a live keynote demo for 1,500+ attendees, and the fourth ContribFest where ~50 contributors worked on real issues.

recent_posts.title: Get a jump on ContribFest with the new web app
recent_posts.summary: Backstage is hosting ContribFest at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon in Amsterdam on March 26, 2026. A new ContribFest web app (contribfest.backstage.io) has been launched to help contributors get started, featuring a local setup checklist, curated issues with filters, a Contrib Champs hall of fame for merged PRs, and a Hall of Hosts. The session also introduces Dev Containers support (via VS Code or IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate with Docker) to streamline environment setup for participants.

recent_posts.title: Backstage Wrapped 2025: Celebrating a mature framework with modern foundations
recent_posts.summary: Backstage celebrated its fifth anniversary in 2025 with major technical advancements. The platform now dominates the internal developer portal market with 89% market share. Key updates include the adoption-ready New Frontend System, deprecation of the old backend system, introduction of the Actions Registry with MCP server support for AI integration, and progress on Backstage UI design system. The community contributed over 7,700 commits to the main repo and 3,300 to community plugins, continuing to expand the ecosystem of adopters, contributors, and plugins.

recent_posts.title: Backstage in Atlanta: Highlights from BackstageCon and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2025
recent_posts.summary: BackstageCon and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2025 took place in Atlanta, featuring talks from organizations like Royal Bank of Canada, Ericsson, Toyota Connected, and Neo4j on scaling Backstage adoption. Key highlights included the release of the adoption-ready New Frontend System, MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for AI-native capabilities, and the third Backstage ContribFest where contributors tackled issues together. The maintainers track celebrated project maturity with stable backend and frontend systems, showcased new features including declarative plugin integration, and outlined the roadmap for Backstage UI and enhanced AI tooling integration.

recent_posts.title: Get ready for Backstage ContribFest at KubeCon!
recent_posts.summary: Backstage will host a ContribFest session at KubeCon 2025 North America in Atlanta on November 13. ContribFest is a 75-minute hands-on track where CNCF projects work with contributors, welcoming both new and experienced participants. To prepare, attendees should fork the Backstage and Backstage Community Plugins repositories, install Node.js version 22 and Yarn, and test their setup by running both codebases locally. The session provides an opportunity to contribute to Backstage with guidance from project experts.

recent_posts.title: Migrating legacy services to a modern developer portal: A technical guide to Backstage integration
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide detailing the migration from legacy service catalogs to Backstage, covering automated migration scripts using GitHub Apps, JWT authentication, and Base64 processing. The post explores adoption challenges including team resistance and lack of understanding, along with strategies like clear roadmaps, personalized demos, and feature additions such as Tech Radar and linter plugins. Key technical aspects include creating catalog-info.yaml files, using entity providers, and implementing scaffolders for streamlined service management.

recent_posts.title: From Zero to Maintainer: My Open Source Journey with Backstage
recent_posts.summary: The author shares their journey from a novice contributor to a maintainer in the Backstage open source project. Starting as a student intern with minimal exposure to the tech stack, they gradually built their skills through hands-on experience and community engagement. They navigated challenges such as understanding Git and contributing meaningful features, eventually taking on more substantial roles and responsibilities within the community.

recent_posts.title: Backstage in London: Highlights from BackstageCon and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2025
recent_posts.summary: BackstageCon and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2025 in London were major events for the Backstage community. The conference featured discussions on Backstage's adoption, its integration with various technologies, and an extensive talk by core maintainers about Backstage's developments. Highlights included sessions on enhanced templates, AI asset cataloging, and automated testing. It also marked the five-year anniversary of Backstage, celebrating its journey and innovations.

recent_posts.title: Backstage Wrapped 2024: The year's Top 5 milestones and highlights
recent_posts.summary: Backstage Wrapped 2024 highlights significant accomplishments including over 60k contributions from a global community, the release of 210+ open source plugins, 278 companies adopting the platform, the launch of the Certified Backstage Associate certification, and the milestone release of the new backend system version 1.0. The Backstage community also celebrated winning the InfoWorld 2024 Technology of the Year Award.

recent_posts.title: The 2024 Backstage Security Audit
recent_posts.summary: Backstage's security stance remains robust after completing its second independent security audit conducted by X41 D-Sec, sponsored by OSTIF under CNCF's guidance. The audit identified and remedied several high and medium severity vulnerabilities. Improvements included secure coding practices and the Backstage Threat Model. Recommendations for handling user sign-in have been updated to enhance security while maintaining ease of use. The audit reflects the ongoing maturity of the Backstage project.
